bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can submit a replication rule whose persisted comment contains HTML or script. The rule-detail page fetched all rule metadata and concatenated every returned key and value into a jQuery-created HTML row before appending it to #t_metadata; therefore the returned comments value was parsed as markup and executed in the WebUI origin when a user opened /ui/rule. The approval page independently passed the unescaped comments property to DataTables, giving administrators a second stored-XSS trigger while reviewing pending rules.
flaw_origin: Commit 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js and the rule-detail view with the generic unsafe sink $('#t_metadata').append($('' + key + '' + data[key] + '')). Commit cebd5b059e8c4629a3ae0b2eccfd922ab906ebd7 later added the persisted rule comment field to the already-unsafe metadata path, and commit 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f later added the separate raw-comments DataTables sink on approve_rules.js. The original 2014 sink, rather than either later source-enablement or sink-copy commit, is the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable rendering mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names human author Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch> and human committer Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch>; its message contains only the RUCIO issue subject and Change-Id: Icbf03845a630afd85d9026d74ec036f5e09daf74, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-rwj9-7j48-9f7q documents POST /proxy/rules/ with an attacker-controlled comment, stored execution at /ui/rule?rule_id=<RULE_ID> and the Approve Rules view, and patched boundaries 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1.

git show 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js shows a new file whose r.list_replication_rule success callback iterates every returned data key and builds a jQuery HTML fragment by concatenating key and data[key], then appends it to #t_metadata without encoding.

git log -L 518,518:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js 24468abb0e076fa83d5f3bc6db6050182fed4c79^ traces the unsafe metadata-row sink through later rewrites back to 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35; 34e9541cfe05327627cf54bbebd5285808835a9b and da5ea0b0b8ab775f89f383587856bb28114688a8 only rewrote the existing mechanism and are not BICs.

git ls-tree -r --name-only ed04270cf7a5f71e451f2a196dba47aa8dc15458 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/rule.html returns no paths, directly proving the BIC's immediate parent lacks both the renderer and its view.

History cross-check: git log -S'comment' over lib/rucio/core/rule.py, lib/rucio/api/rule.py, and lib/rucio/web/rest/rule.py identifies cebd5b059e8c4629a3ae0b2eccfd922ab906ebd7 ('Added comment field to rules') as the later persisted-comment capability; git grep at that commit confirms the API accepts comment and the core stores/returns comments. This connected attacker-controlled stored data to the already-present BIC sink.

The admin trigger is a later copy of the same output-encoding failure: git log -L 78,102:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003^ and -S"{'data': 'comments'" trace filtered_data.push(value) plus the raw comments DataTables column to 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f; that file is absent from its parent db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7.

Canonical mainline direct fix fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c replaces concatenated metadata-row HTML in rule.js with DOM construction and .text(data[sorted_keys[i]]), directly neutralizing the BIC sink. The overall GHSA fix is complete at b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25, which additionally encodes value.comments before the approval DataTable; its message explicitly cites GHSA-rwj9-7j48-9f7q.

Release-branch equivalents are 24468abb0e076fa83d5f3bc6db6050182fed4c79 (rule detail) plus a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 (approval table) for 35.8.3, e8848dfc66f79e5cc9d1077ef371d971dd290db1 plus abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7 for 38.5.4, and 1559c59e1fc571f75775fb4f656d752b32309e24 plus 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41 for 39.3.1. git tag --contains starts those branches at exactly the advisory's patched tags.

Version-boundary git grep proves 35.8.2 (eaebc315c5a4a6721c6744a27a07ad22a9586ff0), 38.5.3 (4fd064e67f4979bf83222a5ad95eb12054e63b59), and 39.3.0 (994beeb0dcad09b75bbb486cf9c58a7d469562e5) still concatenate data[sorted_keys[i]] into HTML, while 35.8.3 (ba9203702629af7bb1f95d5cf9ba8fcf1f943105), 38.5.4 (c851ad216e0e0e3d50405eab3331dfe21c96ddd3), and 39.3.1 (ba2a7e66b1e3c73b5cf9e0000e6621e8dc45bfe7) use .text(data[sorted_keys[i]]) and encode value.comments.

git describe --contains 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 resolves to 0.1.35~51, placing the unsafe renderer years before all affected 35/36/38/39 ranges. The BIC is a normal single-parent commit; an all-ref Change-Id search found only that object, so there is no reconstructable squash/member history to decompose.
git cat-file -p 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 is the sole AI-attribution source used: it shows Thomas Beermann as both author and committer and no AI marker or coauthor/generated trailer.
reasoning: The advisory's stored value is rule.comment/comments, but persistence alone is not the output-encoding bug: execution occurs because server-returned metadata is interpreted as HTML. Tracing the exact rule-detail sink fixed in 2026 reaches the original new-file commit 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35. Later commits that added comments to rule storage, rewrote the same renderer, or copied the flaw into the approval table are lifecycle milestones, not the smallest BIC. The immediate parent has neither rule.js nor rule.html, so parent absence is directly established. The mainline fix converts untrusted values to text nodes in fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c and completes both advisory trigger paths at b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25; equivalent backports appear exactly at all three patched boundaries, while each immediately preceding release retains raw concatenation. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for AI attribution: it is a human-authored/committed 2014 commit with no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
